newsitem.title: UK: CBOT sees enhanced scope for investors from DJIA.
newsitem.headline: CBOT sees enhanced scope for investors from DJIA.

text.p: The introduction of Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) products on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) will open up a new equity product sector to CBOT members, said Patrick Arbor, Chairman CBOT on Friday.
"This event is as significant as the introduction of futures," said Arbor, speaking at a news conference in London.
"The DJIA is the most influential index...and is used as a world-wide benchmark for equity prices."

Dow Jones & Co Inc announced on Thursday that it had licensed the CBOT to offer trading in futures contracts and options on futures contracts based on the DJIA as part of a programme to make the DJIA available to investors for the first time.

Arbor said that subject to approval from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) and the Corporate and Financial Services Commission (CSFC), the CBOT hoped to launch the new products later in the year and to introduce a minimum of six more products over the next two years.
"There will be demand for these products from world-wide investors, particularly from Asia," he said. "A whole new customer base will be exposed."
Richard Sandor, second vice chairman of the CBOT, said the DJIA licensing would add another dimension to the range of CBOT products.
"The CBOT will have all three components for a fund manager to put together a synthetic portfolio, bonds, equities and cash," he said.

He said the other advantages for investors would be that the DJIA products would raise the profile of trading in major capitalised companies listed in the index, and enable price discovery of future dividend flows of U.S. blue chips.
Arbor said the CBOT was pleased with the interest its recent link with the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was attracting.
In early May a link was opened which enables traders to use open outcry to trade the Bund and T-bond futures in both exchanges.
